title: Calculating with Whole Numbers: Order of Operations, Long Multiplication and Long Division
seo_title: Grade 7 Calculating with Whole Numbers Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Perform calculations using all four operations on whole numbers, estimating and using calculators where appropriate; use the order of operations including brackets, squares and cubes; multiply whole numbers by at least 2-digit numbers and divide by at least 2-digit numbers.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 7 worksheets: order of operations with brackets and powers, long multiplication, long division and multi-step problems. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: Estimate to check the size of the answer.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Order of operations: brackets, then powers and roots, then × and ÷ from left to right, then + and − from left to right.
  • Long multiplication: multiply by each digit, write the zeros, then add.
  • Long division: divide, multiply, subtract, bring down.
  • Estimate first to check the size of the answer.

Examples

Example

48 − 3 × (2 + 4)²

brackets: 6

power: 36

3 × 36 = 108

Answer: 48 − 108 = −60

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Left to right only× and ÷ come first.
Ignoring bracketsWork out brackets first.
A missing 0Write 0 when the divisor does not fit.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 7 say about calculations?
faq.a: Add, subtract, multiply and divide whole numbers, including long multiplication and long division, and use the order of operations.

faq.q: How do I check a long division?
faq.a: Multiply the answer by the divisor.

items.q: Work out 3 × 2 − 6 × 2.
items.e: Do both multiplications first: 6 − 12. The answer is −6.

items.q: Work out 4 + 9 × 5.
items.e: Multiply first: 9 × 5 = 45, then 4 + 45. The answer is 49.

items.q: Work out 12 + 7 × 9.
items.e: Multiply first: 7 × 9 = 63, then 12 + 63. The answer is 75.

items.q: Work out 18 + 4 × 4.
items.e: Multiply first: 4 × 4 = 16, then 18 + 16. The answer is 34.

items.q: Work out 14 + 9 × 2.
items.e: Multiply first: 9 × 2 = 18, then 14 + 18. The answer is 32.

items.q: Work out 31 − 2 × 9.
items.e: Multiply first: 2 × 9 = 18, then 31 − 18. The answer is 13.

items.q: Work out 5 × 8 − 5 × 2.
items.e: Do both multiplications first: 40 − 10. The answer is 30.

items.q: Work out 9 + 25 ÷ 5.
items.e: Divide first: 25 ÷ 5 = 5, then 9 + 5. The answer is 14.

items.q: Work out 83 − 9 × 8.
items.e: Multiply first: 9 × 8 = 72, then 83 − 72. The answer is 11.

items.q: Work out 14 + 6 × 2.
items.e: Multiply first: 6 × 2 = 12, then 14 + 12. The answer is 26.

items.q: Work out 2 + 7 × 8.
items.e: Multiply first: 7 × 8 = 56, then 2 + 56. The answer is 58.

items.q: Work out 8 × 7 − 5 × 2.
items.e: Do both multiplications first: 56 − 10. The answer is 46.

items.q: Work out 2 + 42 ÷ 6.
items.e: Divide first: 42 ÷ 6 = 7, then 2 + 7. The answer is 9.

items.q: Work out 10 + 7 × 4.
items.e: Multiply first: 7 × 4 = 28, then 10 + 28. The answer is 38.

items.q: Work out 72 − 7 × 9.
items.e: Multiply first: 7 × 9 = 63, then 72 − 63. The answer is 9.

items.q: Work out 15 − 4 × 2.
items.e: Multiply first: 4 × 2 = 8, then 15 − 8. The answer is 7.

items.q: Work out 6 + 30 ÷ 5.
items.e: Divide first: 30 ÷ 5 = 6, then 6 + 6. The answer is 12.

items.q: Work out 10 + 24 ÷ 6.
items.e: Divide first: 24 ÷ 6 = 4, then 10 + 4. The answer is 14.

items.q: Work out 13 + 28 ÷ 7.
items.e: Divide first: 28 ÷ 7 = 4, then 13 + 4. The answer is 17.

items.q: Work out 3 × 3 − 5 × 2.
items.e: Do both multiplications first: 9 − 10. The answer is −1.
Brackets, then multiply, then add: 8 + 7 × 4. The answer is 36.
Brackets first: 8 + 2 = 10, then 60 ÷ 10. The answer is 6.
Brackets, then multiply, then add: 8 + 5 × 5. The answer is 33.
Brackets first: 9 + 6 = 15, then 135 ÷ 15. The answer is 9.
Brackets, then multiply, then add: 4 + 7 × 6. The answer is 46.
Brackets, then multiply, then add: 3 + 10 × 3. The answer is 33.

items.q: Work out 8 × (2 + 3).
items.e: Brackets first: 2 + 3 = 5, then × 8. The answer is 40.
Brackets first: 16 − 8 = 8, then × 3. The answer is 24.
Brackets first: 3 + 8 = 11, then 99 ÷ 11. The answer is 9.
Brackets first: 13 − 3 = 10, then × 9. The answer is 90.

items.q: Work out 3 + 62.
items.e: Power first: 62 = 36, then 3 + 36. The answer is 39.

items.q: Work out 8 × 32.
items.e: Powers before multiplying: 32 = 9, then 8 × 9. The answer is 72.

items.q: Work out (7 + 4)2.
items.e: Bracket first: 7 + 4 = 11, then 112. The answer is 121.

items.q: Work out 4 + 33.
items.e: Power first: 33 = 27, then 4 + 27. The answer is 31.

items.q: Work out 6 + 32.
items.e: Power first: 32 = 9, then 6 + 9. The answer is 15.

items.q: Work out (4 + 4)2.
items.e: Bracket first: 4 + 4 = 8, then 82. The answer is 64.

items.q: Work out 8 × 43.
items.e: Powers before multiplying: 43 = 64, then 8 × 64. The answer is 512.

items.q: Work out (5 + 1)2.
items.e: Bracket first: 5 + 1 = 6, then 62. The answer is 36.

items.q: Work out 4 × 32.
items.e: Powers before multiplying: 32 = 9, then 4 × 9. The answer is 36.

items.q: Work out (6 + 4)2.
items.e: Bracket first: 6 + 4 = 10, then 102. The answer is 100.

items.q: Use long multiplication.
Calculate 5 180 × 26
items.e: Shortcut: 5 180 = 518 × 10. Work out 518 × 26 = 13 468, then multiply by 10: 134 680. Or use the rows: Row 1: 5 180 × 6 = 31 080. Row 2: 5 180 × 20 = 103 600 (write the place-holder 0, then 5 180 × 2 = 10 360). Add: 31 080 + 103 600 = 134 680.

items.q: Calculate 1 178 × 36
What number goes in the dashed box?
items.e: Add the two rows with column addition, and add every exchanged digit: 49 152 + 552 960 = 602 112.

items.q: What number goes in the dashed box?
items.e: Row 2 multiplies by the tens digit, so it is 6 141 × 30. Write the place-holder 0 first, then 6 141 × 3: 1 × 3 = 3, write 3; 4 × 3 = 12, write 2, exchange 1; 1 × 3 + 1 = 4, write 4; 6 × 3 = 18, write 18. The row is 184 230, not 18 423. Check: 49 128 + 184 230 = 233 358.

items.q: Use long multiplication.
Calculate 1 817 × 37
Calculate 8 771 × 94
What number goes in the dashed box?
items.e: Add the two rows with column addition, and add every exchanged digit: 31 944 + 479 160 = 511 104.

items.q: What number goes in the dashed box?
items.e: Row 2 multiplies by the tens digit, so it is 3 778 × 30. Write the place-holder 0 first, then 3 778 × 3: 8 × 3 = 24, write 4, exchange 2; 7 × 3 + 2 = 23, write 3, exchange 2; 7 × 3 + 2 = 23, write 3, exchange 2; 3 × 3 + 2 = 11, write 11. The row is 113 340, not 11 334. Check: 30 224 + 113 340 = 143 564.

items.q: What number goes in the dashed box?
items.e: Row 1 is 941 × 3: 1 × 3 = 3, write 3; 4 × 3 = 12, write 2, exchange 1; 9 × 3 + 1 = 28, write 28. So the row is 2 823. Check: 2 823 + 65 870 = 68 693.

items.q: Use long multiplication.
What number goes in the dashed box?
items.e: Row 2 multiplies by the tens digit, so it is 156 × 50. Write the place-holder 0 first, then 156 × 5: 6 × 5 = 30, write 0, exchange 3; 5 × 5 + 3 = 28, write 8, exchange 2; 1 × 5 + 2 = 7, write 7. The row is 7 800, not 780. Check: 1 404 + 7 800 = 9 204.

items.q: Calculate 862 × 24
What number goes in the dashed box?
items.e: Row 2 multiplies by the tens digit, so it is 975 × 50. Write the place-holder 0 first, then 975 × 5: 5 × 5 = 25, write 5, exchange 2; 7 × 5 + 2 = 37, write 7, exchange 3; 9 × 5 + 3 = 48, write 48. The row is 48 750, not 4 875. Check: 2 925 + 48 750 = 51 675.

items.q: What number goes in the dashed box?
items.e: Add the two rows with column addition, and add every exchanged digit: 6 958 + 39 760 = 46 718.

items.q: What number goes in the dashed box?
items.e: Row 2 multiplies by the tens digit, so it is 182 × 90. Write the place-holder 0 first, then 182 × 9: 2 × 9 = 18, write 8, exchange 1; 8 × 9 + 1 = 73, write 3, exchange 7; 1 × 9 + 7 = 16, write 16. The row is 16 380, not 1 638. Check: 1 456 + 16 380 = 17 836.

items.q: Use long multiplication.
Use long multiplication.
What number goes in the dashed box?
items.e: Row 2 multiplies by the tens digit, so it is 446 × 50. Write the place-holder 0 first, then 446 × 5: 6 × 5 = 30, write 0, exchange 3; 4 × 5 + 3 = 23, write 3, exchange 2; 4 × 5 + 2 = 22, write 22. The row is 22 300, not 2 230. Check: 892 + 22 300 = 23 192.

items.q: Use long division.
Use long division to work out 4 788 ÷ 59.
items.e: 47 is less than 59, so start with 478. 478 ÷ 59 = 8: 8 × 59 = 472, 478 − 472 = 6. Bring down 8 to make 68: 68 ÷ 59 = 1: 1 × 59 = 59, 68 − 59 = 9. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 9. Answer: 81 r 9. Check: 81 × 59 + 9 = 4 788.

items.q: Use long division to work out 1 513 ÷ 17.
Kabelo works out 1 075 ÷ 28 = 37 r 39. What mistake did he make?
c: He forgot to bring down a digit
He missed a 0 in the answer
items.e: A remainder must be less than the divisor. 39 is more than 28, so 28 goes in once more: 39 − 28 = 11. The answer is 38 r 11. Check: 38 × 28 + 11 = 1 075.

items.q: Use long division.
items.e: 3 is less than 16, so start with 32. 32 ÷ 16 = 2: 2 × 16 = 32, 32 − 32 = 0. Bring down 3 to make 3: 16 does not go into 3, so write 0 in the answer. Bring down 2 to make 32: 32 ÷ 16 = 2: 2 × 16 = 32, 32 − 32 = 0. Answer: 202. Check: 202 × 16 = 3 232.

items.q: Use long division.
items.e: 8 is less than 21, so start with 85. 85 ÷ 21 = 4: 4 × 21 = 84, 85 − 84 = 1. Bring down 4 to make 14: 21 does not go into 14, so write 0 in the answer. Bring down 7 to make 147: 147 ÷ 21 = 7: 7 × 21 = 147, 147 − 147 = 0. Answer: 407. Check: 407 × 21 = 8 547.

items.q: Ofentse works out 6 329 ÷ 48 = 130 r 89. What mistake did she make?
c: She missed a 0 in the answer
She forgot to bring down a digit
items.e: A remainder must be less than the divisor. 89 is more than 48, so 48 goes in once more: 89 − 48 = 41. The answer is 131 r 41. Check: 131 × 48 + 41 = 6 329.

items.q: Use long division to work out 7 553 ÷ 91.
Sibusiso works out 2 160 ÷ 18 = 12. What mistake did he make?
c: He missed a 0 in the answer
He divided the wrong way round
items.e: Check: 12 × 18 = 216, not 2 160. Every digit you bring down needs a digit in the answer, even 0. 2 is less than 18, so start with 21. 21 ÷ 18 = 1: 1 × 18 = 18, 21 − 18 = 3. Bring down 6 to make 36: 36 ÷ 18 = 2: 2 × 18 = 36, 36 − 36 = 0. Bring down 0: there is nothing to divide, so write 0 in the answer. Answer: 120. Check: 120 × 18 = 2 160.

items.q: Use long division to work out 5 071 ÷ 44.
items.e: 5 is less than 44, so start with 50. 50 ÷ 44 = 1: 1 × 44 = 44, 50 − 44 = 6. Bring down 7 to make 67: 67 ÷ 44 = 1: 1 × 44 = 44, 67 − 44 = 23. Bring down 1 to make 231: 231 ÷ 44 = 5: 5 × 44 = 220, 231 − 220 = 11. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 11. Answer: 115 r 11. Check: 115 × 44 + 11 = 5 071.

items.q: You use long division for 936 ÷ 13. The first step is 93 ÷ 13. Which multiple of 13 do you subtract from 93?
items.e: List the multiples of 13: 13, 26, 39, 52, 65, … The largest one that is not more than 93 is 7 × 13 = 91. 93 − 91 = 2. Then bring down the next digit. The whole answer: 936 ÷ 13 = 72.

items.q: Use long division.
What is 609 ÷ 75?
items.e: Round 75 to 80. 609 ÷ 80 is about 7, so try 7. 7 × 75 = 525 and 609 − 525 = 84, which is not less than 75, so 7 is too small. Try 8. 8 × 75 = 600 and 609 − 600 = 9. Answer: 8 r 9. Check: 8 × 75 + 9 = 609.

items.q: Use long division to work out 473 ÷ 43.
What is the remainder when 613 is divided by 27?
items.e: The question asks for the remainder, not the answer to the division. 6 is less than 27, so start with 61. 61 ÷ 27 = 2: 2 × 27 = 54, 61 − 54 = 7. Bring down 3 to make 73: 73 ÷ 27 = 2: 2 × 27 = 54, 73 − 54 = 19. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 19. Answer: 22 r 19. Check: 22 × 27 + 19 = 613.

items.q: What is 367 ÷ 74?
items.e: Round 74 to 70. 367 ÷ 70 is about 5, so try 5. 5 × 74 = 370, which is more than 367, so 5 is too big. Try 4. 4 × 74 = 296 and 367 − 296 = 71. Answer: 4 r 71. Check: 4 × 74 + 71 = 367.

items.q: You use long division for 792 ÷ 18. The first step is 79 ÷ 18. Which multiple of 18 do you subtract from 79?
items.e: List the multiples of 18: 18, 36, 54, 72, 90, … The largest one that is not more than 79 is 4 × 18 = 72. 79 − 72 = 7. Then bring down the next digit. The whole answer: 792 ÷ 18 = 44.

items.q: You use long division for 616 ÷ 28. After 61 − 56 = 5, you bring down the next digit. What do you divide next?
items.e: 61 ÷ 28 = 2. 2 × 28 = 56 and 61 − 56 = 5. Bring down the 6 next to the 5 to make 56. Then 56 ÷ 28 = 2. The whole answer: 22.

items.q: Use long division.
items.e: 7 is less than 18, so start with 71. 71 ÷ 18 = 3: 3 × 18 = 54, 71 − 54 = 17. Bring down 5 to make 175: 175 ÷ 18 = 9: 9 × 18 = 162, 175 − 162 = 13. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 13. Answer: 39 r 13. Check: 39 × 18 + 13 = 715.

items.q: Use long division.
items.e: 9 is less than 68, so start with 99. 99 ÷ 68 = 1: 1 × 68 = 68, 99 − 68 = 31. Bring down 7 to make 317: 317 ÷ 68 = 4: 4 × 68 = 272, 317 − 272 = 45. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 45. Answer: 14 r 45. Check: 14 × 68 + 45 = 997.

items.q: A garden centre has 57 trays of plants. Each tray holds 36 plants. How many plants is that?
items.e: Equal groups: 57 trays × 36 plants, so multiply 36 × 57. Row 1: 36 × 7 = 252. Row 2: 36 × 50 = 1 800 (write the place-holder 0, then 36 × 5 = 180). Add: 252 + 1 800 = 2 052.

items.q: The school kitchen serves 281 lunches each week. How many lunches does it serve in 38 weeks?
items.e: Equal groups: 38 weeks × 281 lunches, so multiply 281 × 38. Row 1: 281 × 8 = 2 248. Row 2: 281 × 30 = 8 430 (write the place-holder 0, then 281 × 3 = 843). Add: 2 248 + 8 430 = 10 678.

items.q: A coach has 53 seats. It is full on every one of its 24 trips to the seaside this summer. How many passengers is that altogether?
items.e: Equal groups: 24 trips × 53 passengers, so multiply 53 × 24. Row 1: 53 × 4 = 212. Row 2: 53 × 20 = 1 060 (write the place-holder 0, then 53 × 2 = 106). Add: 212 + 1 060 = 1 272.

items.q: A factory makes 2 246 toy cars each day. How many toy cars does it make in 24 days?
items.e: Equal groups: 24 days × 2 246 toy cars, so multiply 2 246 × 24. Row 1: 2 246 × 4 = 8 984. Row 2: 2 246 × 20 = 44 920 (write the place-holder 0, then 2 246 × 2 = 4 492). Add: 8 984 + 44 920 = 53 904.

items.q: Kabelo says 3 164 × 47 = 148 708. Estimate to check. Is his answer sensible?
items.e: 3 164 rounds to 3 000 and 47 rounds to 50. 3 000 × 50 = 150 000. 148 708 is close to 150 000, so the answer is sensible. (It is also exactly right.)

items.q: A theatre has 1 615 seats. Every seat is sold for all 26 shows of the Christmas pantomime. How many tickets are sold?
items.e: Equal groups: 26 shows × 1 615 tickets, so multiply 1 615 × 26. Row 1: 1 615 × 6 = 9 690. Row 2: 1 615 × 20 = 32 300 (write the place-holder 0, then 1 615 × 2 = 3 230). Add: 9 690 + 32 300 = 41 990.

items.q: Sarah says 689 × 52 = 35 828. Estimate to check. Is her answer sensible?
items.e: 689 rounds to 700 and 52 rounds to 50. 700 × 50 = 35 000. 35 828 is close to 35 000, so the answer is sensible. (It is also exactly right.)

items.q: A farm packs 144 eggs in each crate. It sends 26 crates on Monday and 38 crates on Tuesday. How many eggs does it send altogether?
Sipho says 4 127 × 63 = 12 381. Estimate to check. Is his answer sensible?
items.e: 4 127 rounds to 4 000 and 63 rounds to 60. 4 000 × 60 = 240 000. 12 381 is far from 240 000, so the answer cannot be right. The correct answer is 260 001; Sipho only multiplied by the ones digit.

items.q: Pieter swims 64 lengths of a 25 m pool over a term. How far does he swim?
items.e: Equal groups: 64 lengths × 25 m, so multiply 64 × 25. Row 1: 64 × 5 = 320. Row 2: 64 × 20 = 1 280 (write the place-holder 0, then 64 × 2 = 128). Add: 320 + 1 280 = 1 600.

items.q: A train travels 742 km in 14 hours. It goes the same distance every hour. How far does it travel each hour?
items.e: Divide: 7 is less than 14, so start with 74. 74 ÷ 14 = 5: 5 × 14 = 70, 74 − 70 = 4. Bring down 2 to make 42: 42 ÷ 14 = 3: 3 × 14 = 42, 42 − 42 = 0. So 742 ÷ 14 = 53. There is no remainder, so the answer is 53 km.

items.q: A pizza restaurant shares 33 pizzas equally between 24 children at a party. How much pizza does each child get?
items.e: Divide: 3 is less than 24, so start with 33. 33 ÷ 24 = 1: 1 × 24 = 24, 33 − 24 = 9. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 9. So 33 ÷ 24 = 1 r 9. The remainder can be shared too: 9 pizzas ÷ 24 = 924 pizza. Simplify: 924 = 38. Each gets 1 38 pizzas.

items.q: A class raises R1 047 at a cake sale. The money is shared equally between 25 charities. How much does each charity get?
items.e: Divide: 10 is less than 25, so start with 104. 104 ÷ 25 = 4: 4 × 25 = 100, 104 − 100 = 4. Bring down 7 to make 47: 47 ÷ 25 = 1: 1 × 25 = 25, 47 − 25 = 22. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 22. So 1 047 ÷ 25 = 41 r 22. Money can be shared into cents, so write the remainder as a decimal: R22 ÷ 25 = R0,88. Each share is R41,88.

items.q: 54 bars of chocolate are shared equally between 21 learners. How many bars does each learner get?
items.e: Divide: 5 is less than 21, so start with 54. 54 ÷ 21 = 2: 2 × 21 = 42, 54 − 42 = 12. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 12. So 54 ÷ 21 = 2 r 12. The remainder can be shared too: 12 bars ÷ 21 = 1221 bar. Simplify: 1221 = 47. Each gets 2 47 bars.

items.q: A garden centre has 1 813 bulbs. It packs them in bags of 36 and fills as many bags as it can. How many bulbs are not in a bag?
items.e: Divide: 18 is less than 36, so start with 181. 181 ÷ 36 = 5: 5 × 36 = 180, 181 − 180 = 1. Bring down 3 to make 13: 36 does not go into 13, so write 0 in the answer. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 13. So 1 813 ÷ 36 = 50 r 13. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 13 bulbs.

items.q: A rope is 1 535 cm long. It is cut into 25 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: Divide: 15 is less than 25, so start with 153. 153 ÷ 25 = 6: 6 × 25 = 150, 153 − 150 = 3. Bring down 5 to make 35: 35 ÷ 25 = 1: 1 × 25 = 25, 35 − 25 = 10. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 10. So 1 535 ÷ 25 = 61 r 10. Lengths can be split into parts, so write the remainder as a decimal: 1025 = 10 ÷ 25 = 0,4. Each piece is 61,4 cm, not 61,10 cm.

items.q: A ferry carries 26 cars on each crossing. 591 cars are waiting in the car park. How many crossings are needed to take every car?
items.e: Divide: 5 is less than 26, so start with 59. 59 ÷ 26 = 2: 2 × 26 = 52, 59 − 52 = 7. Bring down 1 to make 71: 71 ÷ 26 = 2: 2 × 26 = 52, 71 − 52 = 19. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 19. So 591 ÷ 26 = 22 r 19. 22 crossings are not enough: 19 cars would still be waiting. You need 1 more, so the answer is 23 crossings.

items.q: 15 friends share a holiday cottage that costs R1 416. They each pay the same amount. How much does each person pay?
items.e: Divide: 14 is less than 15, so start with 141. 141 ÷ 15 = 9: 9 × 15 = 135, 141 − 135 = 6. Bring down 6 to make 66: 66 ÷ 15 = 4: 4 × 15 = 60, 66 − 60 = 6. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 6. So 1 416 ÷ 15 = 94 r 6. Money can be shared into cents, so write the remainder as a decimal: R6 ÷ 15 = R0,40. Each share is R94,40.

items.q: There are 211 people coming to a summer fair lunch. Each table seats 16 people. How many tables are needed so everyone has a seat?
items.e: Divide: 2 is less than 16, so start with 21. 21 ÷ 16 = 1: 1 × 16 = 16, 21 − 16 = 5. Bring down 1 to make 51: 51 ÷ 16 = 3: 3 × 16 = 48, 51 − 48 = 3. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 3. So 211 ÷ 16 = 13 r 3. 13 tables are not enough: 3 people would still need a seat. You need 1 more, so the answer is 14 tables.

items.q: A farm collected 2 223 eggs. It packs them in boxes of 12. How many boxes can it fill completely?
items.e: Divide: 2 is less than 12, so start with 22. 22 ÷ 12 = 1: 1 × 12 = 12, 22 − 12 = 10. Bring down 2 to make 102: 102 ÷ 12 = 8: 8 × 12 = 96, 102 − 96 = 6. Bring down 3 to make 63: 63 ÷ 12 = 5: 5 × 12 = 60, 63 − 60 = 3. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 3. So 2 223 ÷ 12 = 185 r 3. The 3 eggs left over are not enough to fill another box, so ignore the remainder. The answer is 185 boxes.
